card.line: Migdol, meaning "tower," is a name used for places on Egypt's edge. One was near where Israel camped by the sea, and a city of that name is named in warnings about Egypt.

moments.title: Camp Near Migdol
moments.text: God told Moses to have the Israelites turn back and camp by the sea, between Migdol and the sea. Pharaoh would think they were boxed in, and God would gain honor over him.

moments.title: A Stop on the Journey
moments.text: Israel set out from Etham, turned back to Pi-hahiroth, and camped near Migdol. From there they crossed through the sea into the wilderness.

moments.title: Jews Living in Egypt
moments.text: God's word came to Jeremiah about the Jews living in Egypt, including those in Migdol. God reminded them that Jerusalem lay in ruins because of the evil of the people.

moments.title: Warning of Babylon's Sword
moments.text: God told Jeremiah to announce in Egypt, and to proclaim in Migdol and other cities, that Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon was coming against Egypt. Egypt's warriors would fall.

moments.title: From Migdol to Syene
moments.text: God said He would turn Egypt into a ruin, an empty wasteland from Migdol to Syene. He said Egypt's allies would fall by the sword, from Migdol to Syene.
